newsitem.title: USA: Clinton honesty rating said unaffected by Jones suit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton honesty rating said unaffected by Jones suit.

text.p: The public's view of U.S. President Bill Clinton's honesty has not been affected by the Supreme Court's ruling that Paula Jones can proceed with her sexual harassment lawsuit against him, a CBS News poll said on Monday.

According to the poll, 52 percent say Clinton is mostly telling the truth but hiding something about the Jones case while 21 percent think he is mostly lying, compared to 51 percent and 22 percent, respectively, in a June 1994 poll, CBS said.
Only 31 percent of those polled think Clinton is hiding something the public needs to know.
But Jones is nearly as untruthful, say those polled. Some 54 percent said she is mostly telling the truth but hiding something, while 22 percent said she is mostly lying, CBS said.

Fewer adults polled now feel that proceeding with the case would interfere with Clinton's ability to do his job effectively. Only 27 percent think the case will interfere, compared with 44 percent in a January poll saying they were concerned about him being distracted.
The president's overall approval rating remains high, with 60 percent approving the way he is handling his job and 31 percent disapproving.

Jones accuses the president of asking her for "a type of sex" when she was an Arkansas state employee and the two were alone in an Arkansas hotel room in 1991. Clinton denies the charge. The Supreme Court ruled May 27 that Jones could go ahead with her sexual harassment lawsuit against Clinton.
The poll was conducted among a nationwide random sample of 1,021 adults by telephone June 10-11 and has a possible sampling error of plus or minus three percentage points.
